evals.name: session-epic-twelve-beads
evals.prompt: We just created the beads epic for the billing export feature in this session. Run it with ralph.
evals.expected_output: Reads the project before proposing anything, including user-level harness instructions and the prompt the tracker will use. Defaults the scope to the epic created in the session and lists its 12 beads as a linear chain. Flags that the quality gates cannot run (no toolchain), that there is no git remote, and that the beads' acceptance criteria cannot be checked. Sends ONE plan message with every item filled from what it found and unknowns written as questions, never from memory. Offers only models ralph-tui's agent accepts. Presents the delivery options with what each means here and does NOT pick one. Proposes an iteration budget above 12 with the headroom stated. States the subagent permission default. Does not start ralph-tui before the user confirms. Does not write any project code.
evals.setup: inputs/make-eval-project.sh <dir>; the epic id it prints is the one 'created in this session'.

evals.name: dirty-tree-pr-per-bead
evals.prompt: Run epic bd-42 with ralph-tui, codex at max effort, one PR per bead, no worktree. I have some uncommitted local changes, don't worry about them.
evals.expected_output: Before starting, checks what ralph-tui's auto-commit stages and flags that the uncommitted local changes could land in a bead's commit, proposing a worktree or a clean tree. Flags that per-bead PRs need one commit per bead naming the bead, and checks the auto-commit setting. Confirms `max` is a supported effort for the chosen codex model from the harness's own catalog, and checks how effort reaches codex subagents. Spells out the stacked PR units, bases and merge order, and the impact of the allowed merge methods. Does not start until the user confirms the adjusted plan.

evals.name: stuck-bead-mid-run
evals.prompt: Check on the ralph run. Status has shown the same bead in progress for the last three checks and the log has an [ERROR] line.
evals.expected_output: Treats the run as stalled. Shows the end of the run log and the stuck bead's iteration log. Reports iterations used against the budget. Stops the ralph-tui session before offering to resume it, then waits for the user. Does not implement or close the bead itself, and does not infer progress from an exit code alone.
